feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+10y=\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+31\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+10y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +10 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +1)-1+10 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2} & =-9 \\ \lambda +1 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-1\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =-1\pm 3\text{i}$, and therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}={e}^{-x}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+B\operatorname{sin}⁡3x).
$$

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+31\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x,
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x} & =-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡3x+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡3x \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =-9\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x-9\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x\end{aligned}
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
(-9\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x-9\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x)+2(-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡3x+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡3x)+10(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+31\operatorname{sin}⁡3x
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(\alpha +6\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+(-6\alpha +\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡3x=\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+31\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}\alpha +6\beta =1\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3x) \\ -6\alpha +\beta =31\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-5$ and $\beta =1.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-5\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y={e}^{-x}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+B\operatorname{sin}⁡3x)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$
